title: Sell Mineral Rights in West Virginia
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in West Virginia | Marcellus Buyer
metaDescription: West Virginia mineral owners holding an old severed estate in Marcellus or Utica country: we do the deed research a century-old severance usually needs.
heroLead: West Virginia has more hundred-year-old severed mineral deeds than any state the royalty desk reviews, and tracing one of those back to a living owner is half the job.
intro: West Virginia's coal, oil, and gas history goes back well over a century, and a lot of mineral ownership in the state was severed from the surface during that early era, sometimes for a few dollars an acre, long before anyone imagined Marcellus and Utica development. Those old severances got divided among heirs generation after generation, which means the person holding a fractional interest today is often several generations removed from whoever originally sold the minerals off.
That history is exactly why West Virginia title work looks different from a newer state. It's slower, it's more document-heavy, and it's something we've done often enough to move through efficiently.

sections.heading: West Virginia's Old Severed Estates
paragraphs: A severed mineral estate means the mineral rights were split off from surface ownership at some point, sometimes decades before oil and gas development made those minerals valuable. In West Virginia, this frequently happened in the late 1800s or early 1900s tied to coal, timber, or early oil interests, with the mineral portion then passing through generations of heirs, sometimes without anyone updating the county record along the way.
If you've inherited a fractional interest and don't have a clean modern deed, that's completely normal here. We're set up to trace it.

sections.heading: Marcellus Depth vs Utica Depth Rights
paragraphs: Because West Virginia's mineral history predates modern shale development by so long, older deeds sometimes used depth language that wasn't written with the Marcellus or the deeper Utica in mind, or in some cases only conveyed rights to specific formations known at the time. Whether your interest covers both formations, just one, or something more ambiguous depends entirely on the specific deed language.
We read that language carefully, since it determines what you actually have the right to sell and what an operator can develop under an existing lease.

sections.heading: Northern Panhandle vs Southern West Virginia
paragraphs: The Northern Panhandle counties, Marshall, Wetzel, Ohio, sit in some of the most active Marcellus and Utica development in the state, with dense modern horizontal drilling. Southern West Virginia's production leans more toward older, shallower conventional gas wells alongside the region's long coal history. Both regions have real value, but the development pace and well profile differ enough that we price them on separate assumptions.
We ask which part of the state you're in early, since it changes what questions we ask next.

sections.heading: Tracking Down a Century-Old Deed
paragraphs: West Virginia county clerk offices hold deed books going back well over a hundred years, and finding the original severance instrument, then following every subsequent transfer or probate down to you, can take real research time. We handle this as a standard part of our process rather than asking you to produce documents you likely don't have.
If you have even fragments, an old letter, a partial deed, a family name, that's often enough for us to pick up the trail at the courthouse.

faqs.question: Can the royalty desk help when an owner has family knowledge but no West Virginia deed?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is common in West Virginia given how old many severances are. We can typically trace ownership through county clerk records starting from whatever fragments of information you have, a family name, an approximate location, an old document.

faqs.question: Does your old deed cover the Marcellus and the Utica, or just one?
faqs.answer: It depends on the specific depth and formation language in your deed, which can vary widely on older West Virginia instruments. We review this carefully since it determines what rights you actually hold.

faqs.question: Is Northern Panhandle acreage worth more than southern West Virginia?
faqs.answer: Generally the Northern Panhandle has seen denser modern Marcellus and Utica development, which can support stronger near-term value, but southern West Virginia interests with steady conventional production still have real worth. We price against your specific well and history.

faqs.question: How long does title research take on an old West Virginia severed estate?
faqs.answer: It varies with how many generations and transfers are involved, but it's routine work for us. We start it right after an initial conversation so it doesn't hold up your offer any longer than necessary.

faqs.question: Your family owns a small fractional share split among several cousins. Can you buy just your piece?
faqs.answer: Yes, we can typically buy an individual owner's fractional share without requiring every co-owner to sell. We confirm your exact percentage through the deed and probate chain before making an offer.

faqs.question: Does West Virginia coal severance affect your oil and gas mineral rights?
faqs.answer: It can, since some older deeds bundled coal, oil, and gas together while others split them out separately. We read the specific severance language on your deed to confirm what you actually hold before pricing anything.

faqs.question: Can you buy a West Virginia interest that's currently in a dispute among heirs?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, depending on the nature of the dispute. We'll be honest early if a title issue needs to be resolved through probate or court before a clean sale can close, rather than taking your file and letting it stall out later.
